howWeWork.headline: Diagnose · Configure · Live.
howWeWork.intro: We start by deciding together whether automation actually solves your problem. If it doesn't, we tell you. If it does, you walk out with a written plan.

diagnose.title: Diagnose
diagnose.body: A 30-minute call with your team to look at the operation honestly and decide together whether automation actually solves your problem. If it doesn't, we tell you straight. If it does, you walk out with a written plan: which workflows, which integrations, what it'll cost, what to expect.

configure.title: Configure
configure.body: We build your agent end-to-end: integrations with the tools you already use, training on your real data, personalization to your voice and rules. You review every sprint. Nothing goes live until you sign off.

goLive.title: Go Live
goLive.body: Your agent goes into production. We monitor it 24/7, measure performance against the metrics we agreed in the diagnostic, and improve it monthly. You see the dashboard. Your team focuses on the work that needs a human.

pullQuote.text: We build, run and improve the AI agent your team needs — without you having to hire anyone new.

qualifier.headline: Built for teams that already feel the bottleneck.

yes.yes1: Your team is losing real hours every week to repetitive customer interactions — booking, follow-up, status questions, post-sale support.
yes.yes2: You're past the "can AI help?" stage and ready for an agent that runs in production with measurable results in weeks, not quarters.
yes.yes3: You've tried no-code or off-the-shelf chatbots (Zapier, Make, Intercom flows) and they broke the moment volume or edge cases showed up.
yes.yes4: You'd rather get a working agent we operate for you than another tool, codebase or contractor to manage.

qualifier.noTitle: This is NOT for you if…

no.no1: You're shopping purely on price. Our floor is $850 setup + $120/mo — there are cheaper templates if that's the priority.
no.no2: You need someone live tomorrow. Our diagnostic slots open 2–3 weeks out and we don't cut corners on scoping.

faq.headline: Questions everyone asks.
faq.intro: If yours isn't here, drop it in the diagnostic call.

cost.a: Every engagement starts with a free 30-minute diagnostic call. If we both agree to move forward, you pick a tier: Essential ($850 setup + $120/mo), Pro ($1,490 + $249/mo, where most teams land) or Business 360 ($2,990 + $390/mo). USD, taxes excluded. 50% on signing, 50% on kickoff. 10% off when billed annually.

timing.q: How long until the agent is live?
timing.a: Most agents go live 3 to 4 weeks after kickoff — up to 6 weeks if integrations are heavy or your data needs cleanup first. The diagnostic gives you the exact timeline (and the milestones) in writing before you commit to setup.

codeOwnership.a: No — and that's by design. Your agent runs on infrastructure we monitor and improve 24/7. You own everything that actually matters: your data, conversation history, integrations, business rules, and the agent's logic and tone. You can export all of it at any time. What you don't get is a codebase to maintain, hire for, or babysit. That's our job.

leaving.q: What if we want to leave?
leaving.a: Cancel any month after the first 3, with 30 days' notice. We export your data, conversation history and configuration in standard formats. If you're moving to another vendor, we help with the handoff. No clawbacks, no contractual lock-in.

compliance.q: Is our data safe? GDPR / CCPA?
compliance.a: Yes. EU-hosted infrastructure for European clients (GDPR-compliant by default). DPA signed before any real data touches our systems. Your data is never used to train models we sell to other clients. SOC 2 Type 1 in progress, target Q3 2026.

channels.q: Which channels and tools do you integrate with?
channels.a: Out of the box: WhatsApp Business, Instagram DM, web chat, email, Google Calendar, Outlook, Stripe, Cal.com, HubSpot, common PMS / CRM / booking systems, and most no-code platforms (Make, n8n, Zapier). Anything with a documented API is fair game — the diagnostic confirms the exact list before you sign.

engineer.q: Do we need an in-house engineer to manage this?
engineer.a: No. That's the entire point. You get a working agent and a dashboard. Operations, monitoring, model upgrades and the monthly improvement cycle are on us. Your team only does the work that genuinely needs a human.

metrics.q: What do you actually measure — and how do we know it's working?
metrics.a: We agree on 2 to 3 outcome metrics during the diagnostic — usually something like response time, resolution rate, no-shows recovered, or cost per handled conversation. From day one you see them live in your dashboard, alongside conversation logs you can audit. If a metric drifts, the next improvement cycle prioritizes fixing it.

nda.a: Yes — but not for the first call. Our standard MSA + DPA cover most clients. We sign custom NDAs for regulated industries (healthcare, financial services, legal) on request, no friction.

different.q: How do we know you're different from another AI agency?
different.a: Two ways to test it. One: ask for a 15-minute reference call with a live client before you commit — we'll arrange it. Two: the diagnostic itself. An agency that wants to sell at any cost doesn't tell clients to walk away — we do, when it's the right call. Shipping something the wrong client won't use is worse for both sides.

noNeed.q: What if the diagnostic concludes we don't need you?
noNeed.a: We tell you straight and you keep whatever notes and recommendations came out of the call to act on however you want — in-house, with another vendor, or shelved for later. We'd rather lose one deal than ship something that won't earn its keep. Long term, that's the only marketing that scales.

finalCta.subheadline: You'll talk to an engineer, not a salesperson. We leave with a go/no-go — yours or ours.
finalCta.microcopy: Don't see a slot that works? Email contacto@auphere.com and we'll find one.

meta.title: Privacy
meta.description: How Auphere collects, uses and protects personal data — GDPR, CCPA and LGPD aligned.

header.title: How we handle data — yours, and your customers'.
header.intro: This policy describes what Auphere collects, why, where it lives, who can touch it, and how long we keep it. It applies to auphere.com, to clients of our managed agent service, and to people who interact with agents we operate.

controller.title: Who we are
controller.p1: Auphere is the controller of the personal data described in this policy. For any privacy question, write to privacy@auphere.com — we read every message and reply within 30 days.
controller.p2: If you are a resident of the European Economic Area, the United Kingdom or Switzerland, you have the right to lodge a complaint with your local supervisory authority — we'll cooperate fully.

dataCollected.title: Data we collect
dataCollected.intro: We collect only what we need to run the site, evaluate fit on a diagnostic call, deliver the service, and meet legal obligations. Three groups of people, three buckets of data:

visitors.description: Privacy-respecting analytics (Plausible) — no cookies, no cross-site tracking, no personal identifiers. We aggregate page views, referrers and country (never IP).

leads.term: People who book a call or email us
leads.description: Name, work email, company, the message you sent, and the call recording if you opt in. We use it to evaluate fit and reply. We never sell it.

clients.description: Whatever your contract says we process on your behalf — conversation logs, integration metadata, configuration. We are a processor for this data; you are the controller. A DPA is signed before any real data is touched.

consent.description: You give it when you opt into a call recording or subscribe to anything we offer. You can withdraw it at any time.

contract.description: To deliver the diagnostic, the agent setup and the ongoing managed service we agreed in writing.

legitimate.description: To run the website, fight abuse, evaluate inbound leads, and improve the agents we operate — provided your fundamental rights are not overridden.

legal.description: Tax, accounting, regulatory inquiries. We retain only what the law requires, only for as long as it requires.

subProcessors.title: Sub-processors
subProcessors.intro: We use a small list of vetted vendors to deliver the service. Each one is bound by a DPA and processes only the data described next to its name. We update this list when it changes.

vercel.description: Hosts auphere.com and our admin tooling. No client production data.

railway.description: Runs the API and worker that power the managed agents.

postgres.description: Primary store for client data. Tenant isolation enforced at the row level.

anthropic.description: LLM provider (Claude Sonnet 4.6, Haiku 4.5). Data is not used to train Anthropic models — zero-retention API.

openai.description: Fallback LLM provider (GPT-4o). Same zero-retention API terms.

ycloud.description: WhatsApp Business Solution Provider — used only for clients with a WhatsApp channel.

composio.description: OAuth broker for integrations (Calendar, CRM, etc.). We hold the credentials; Composio brokers the connection.

browserbase.description: Headless browser sessions for booking on third-party panels — used only when the agent must operate a vendor UI.

langfuse.description: LLM observability — traces, evaluations and improvement cycles.

plausible.description: Privacy-respecting analytics for auphere.com. No cookies, no cross-site tracking.

resend.description: Transactional email for diagnostic confirmations and operational notifications.

cal.description: Booking scheduling for the diagnostic call.

retention.title: How long we keep things
retention.p2: Diagnostic call data (notes, recording if you opted in): 12 months, then deleted unless we sign an agreement.
retention.p3: Client production data: for the duration of the contract, plus a 30-day window after termination for export, then permanent deletion (audit log retained as required by law).

rights.title: Your rights
rights.intro: Regardless of jurisdiction, we will honour the following on request. Write to privacy@auphere.com.

access.description: Get a copy of everything we hold on you.

erase.description: Have it deleted, subject to legal retention requirements.

portability.description: Get your data in a standard, machine-readable format.

object.description: Tell us to stop processing data under legitimate interest.

ccpa.description: We don't sell personal information. You can confirm this in writing on request.

transfers.title: International transfers
transfers.p1: When data leaves the EU, we rely on Standard Contractual Clauses (SCCs) and on each vendor's transfer mechanism. EU clients can request EU-only processing — we honour it for everything except providers without an EU region (clearly listed above).

cookies.title: Cookies
cookies.p1: auphere.com sets only strictly necessary cookies. Plausible uses no cookies at all. If we ever change that, you'll see a consent banner before anything is dropped.

contact.title: Contact
contact.p1: Questions, requests, complaints: privacy@auphere.com. We reply within 30 days, often the same week.

meta.title: Terms
meta.description: The contract for Auphere's diagnostic, setup and managed agent service. Bespoke + managed — code stays with us, your data stays yours.

header.title: The contract, in plain English.
header.intro: These terms govern the diagnostic call, the agent setup and the ongoing managed service we deliver. They apply alongside the Master Services Agreement (MSA) and Data Processing Agreement (DPA) we sign before any real data is processed.

service.title: What we deliver
service.p1: Auphere operates a bespoke AI agent service in three phases: a diagnostic call (free, 30 minutes), an agent setup (one-time, scoped in writing), and an ongoing managed service (monthly fee, the agent runs on our infrastructure under an SLA).
service.p2: We are not a SaaS vendor. We are not a software contractor that hands over a codebase. The relationship is the operation — we run the agent for you for as long as the contract is in force.

diagnostic.title: The diagnostic
diagnostic.p1: The diagnostic is a 30-minute conversation with an engineer. There is no cost and no commitment. We leave with a written go/no-go: which workflows would automate, which integrations would be needed, an estimate, and a timeline.
diagnostic.p2: If we conclude automation does not solve your problem, we say so and the relationship ends there. You keep our notes.

bespoke.title: Bespoke + managed
bespoke.p1: Once you sign, we configure the agent to your real operation — your tools, your voice, your rules. Setup is a one-time fee, scoped in writing, paid 50% on signing and 50% on kickoff. The agent goes live only when you sign off on the configuration.
bespoke.p2: From go-live, the agent runs under a monthly managed service: we host it, monitor it 24/7, fix what breaks, and improve it on an agreed cycle (monthly, bi-weekly or weekly depending on tier).

code.title: Code and infrastructure ownership
code.p1: The agent runs on infrastructure operated by Auphere. The codebase, models, prompts, orchestration logic and underlying platform belong to Auphere — not to the client.
code.p2: This is deliberate. You buy a working agent and a service, not a codebase to maintain, hire engineers for, or babysit. That is our job.

clientData.title: What is yours
clientData.p1: Your data is yours. Your conversation history is yours. Your business rules, your integrations, the agent's configuration and the tone of voice we tuned to your brand — all yours. You can export them at any time, in standard formats.
clientData.p2: Auphere never uses your data to train models we sell to other clients. The DPA we sign codifies this.

fees.title: Fees and billing
fees.p1: Prices are in USD, taxes excluded. Setup is paid 50% on contract signing, 50% on project kickoff. The managed service is invoiced monthly (or annually, with a 10% discount).
fees.p2: If usage exceeds the contracted volume (conversations, integrations), we agree the next tier before the next billing cycle — no surprise invoices.

cancellation.title: Cancellation
cancellation.p1: You may cancel the managed service any month after the first three, with 30 days' written notice. There are no clawbacks and no contractual lock-in beyond the initial 3-month minimum.
cancellation.p2: On termination, we provide a 30-day export window during which we export your data, conversation history and configuration in standard formats. If you are moving to another vendor, we help with the handoff. After the export window, we delete all client data except what we are legally required to retain.

confidentiality.title: Confidentiality and NDAs
confidentiality.p1: Both sides treat the other's confidential information as confidential, period. Our standard MSA covers this for most engagements. We sign custom NDAs for regulated industries (healthcare, financial services, legal) on request, with no friction.

sla.title: Service levels
sla.p1: Each tier ships with an SLA, written into the contract. Business 360 includes a 4-hour response window for production incidents.
sla.p2: We measure outcome metrics agreed during the diagnostic (response time, resolution rate, no-shows recovered, cost per handled conversation). You see them live in your dashboard. If a metric drifts, the next improvement cycle prioritises fixing it.

liability.title: Liability
liability.p1: Our aggregate liability is capped at the fees paid to Auphere in the twelve months preceding the claim. We exclude indirect and consequential damages to the extent permitted by law.
liability.p2: These caps do not apply to indemnities for confidentiality breaches, willful misconduct or the breach of data protection obligations — the MSA spells out the carve-outs.

law.title: Governing law
law.p1: Unless your MSA says otherwise, these terms are governed by the law of Spain. EU clients may elect to be governed by the law of their habitual residence for consumer-protection purposes.

meta.title: Trust & Security
meta.description: How Auphere isolates client data, where it lives, who can touch it, and what we do when something goes wrong.

header.title: Compliance-by-design. Not check-the-box.
header.intro: Where data lives, how tenants are isolated, what gets encrypted, who can touch what, and what happens when something goes wrong. The architecture, not the marketing.

hosting.title: Where data lives
hosting.p1: Our production runtime is hosted on infrastructure in the European Union by default. EU clients get EU-only processing on request, with the exception of vendors that do not offer an EU region (those are listed in the privacy policy with their region).
hosting.p2: US-only or LATAM-only processing is available for clients with regulatory requirements that demand it, on a per-contract basis.

rls.description: Each tenant's data is partitioned at the database level. Tenant context is scoped automatically on every query — application code cannot accept a tenant ID from a caller, by design.

tools.description: Each agent ships with an explicit allow-list of tools and integrations. Even if a model tried to call something outside the list, the runtime rejects the call before it hits a third party.

models.description: Your conversation data is never used to train models we sell to other clients. We use zero-retention APIs with our LLM providers.

encryption.title: Encryption
encryption.p1: All data is encrypted in transit (TLS 1.3) and at rest (AES-256 on managed-database storage). Secrets are managed in Doppler and rotated on a schedule.
encryption.p2: Backups are encrypted with the same controls and retained for 30 days.

access.title: Who can access what
access.p1: Access to client data is restricted to the engineers actively delivering or supporting that client's agent — a small, named list per engagement. All access is logged.
access.p2: Engineers use named accounts, hardware MFA and short-lived credentials. No shared accounts. No password reuse across systems.

gdpr.description: EU-hosted by default. DPA signed before any real data touches our systems. Sub-processors listed in the privacy policy.

ccpa.description: We do not sell personal information. California residents can exercise CCPA rights via privacy@auphere.com.

lgpd.description: Brazilian clients can request LGPD-aligned processing — same operational guarantees as GDPR, contract amendments as needed.

soc2.description: Audit in progress. Target completion Q3 2026. We share our security questionnaire and current controls on request under NDA.

subprocessors.title: Sub-processors
subprocessors.p1: The full, up-to-date list of sub-processors is published in our privacy policy with the region and purpose for each one. We notify clients in advance of any change.

incident.title: If something goes wrong
incident.p1: We commit to notify affected clients of any confirmed security incident within 72 hours of discovery, with what we know at that point and how we are responding.
incident.p2: We run blameless postmortems for any production incident with material impact and share the relevant findings with clients.

vuln.title: Reporting a vulnerability
vuln.p1: If you believe you have found a security issue, write to security@auphere.com. We acknowledge within 1 business day, fix verified issues without ceremony, and credit reporters who want the recognition.
